claim_gate.best_peer_rule: Superior is always relative to the best peer for that cell among peers that support the cell's capability and have a runnable driver. Peers without a driver, and peers lacking the capability, are listed as excluded, never counted.
claim_gate.superior_rule: Throughput: paired 95% CI lower bound of the partitionline/peer ratio above 1.0. Latency: CI upper bound of each percentile ratio below 1.0 at every declared load.

claim_types.requirement: superior in every required cell of all six contract profiles plus the required compressed cells (lz4, zstd), on both x86_64 and arm64, independently reproduced (KL04-14); no exceptions
superior in every required cell of that profile on that architecture, independently reproduced
paired 95% CI lower bound of the throughput ratio at least 1+X in every covered cell; latency percentile ratio CI upper bound at most 1-X
CPU-per-record ratio CI upper bound at most 0.80 against the best peer; never worded as fastest
throughput ratio CI lower bound at least 1.20, or CPU-per-record CI upper bound at most 0.80, with p99 ratio CI upper bound at most 1.05 at matched load

equal_semantics.description: A benchmark comparison is strictly invalid if durability/acks/idempotence/isolation/security differ. All comparison pairs must match across the frozen required match fields.
rules: Durability, min.insync.replicas, replication factor, and broker ISR topology must match across all compared peers.
Producer acks level (0, 1, or -1/all) must be identical across compared clients.
Idempotence must be identically configured (both enabled or both disabled); when enabled, max.in.flight.requests.per.connection must be bounded <= 5.
Consumer isolation.level (read_uncommitted vs read_committed) must match across all compared clients.
Security protocol (PLAINTEXT, SSL/TLS, SASL_PLAINTEXT, SASL_SSL) and authentication mechanism (PLAIN, SCRAM-SHA-256, SCRAM-SHA-512, OAUTHBEARER) must match.
Enqueue acceptance (e.g. try_send returning Ok) is local buffering and must not be counted as broker acknowledgment; only broker produce responses count as acked.
Broker acknowledgment is not proof of a per-record fsync; fsync depends on broker log.flush configuration and OS page cache writeback.
High-watermark and count equality are necessary baseline assertions, but insufficient to establish exactly-once delivery; record payload and ID integrity must be verified.

warmup.description: Warmup traffic must run prior to steady-state measurement to stabilize JIT, TCP connection caches, and broker thread pools. All warmup records are discarded from steady-state percentiles and throughput totals.

repetitions.order: randomized A/B or Latin square per repetition
repetitions.description: At least five paired randomized repetitions per cell to neutralize temporal drift, background noise, and host thermal throttling.

duration.description: Each steady-state repetition must run for at least 60 seconds or until the sample floor is satisfied.

sample_floor.description: Strict sample floor required before computing percentiles or statistical aggregates.

uncertainty.method: 95% bootstrap confidence interval and median +- MAD (Median Absolute Deviation)
uncertainty.description: All published comparative results must report uncertainty intervals. Single-run peak values or unanchored point estimates are prohibited.

failed_run_policy.rule: A failed cell stays failed; rerun success does not erase it; no progress-string success.
triggers: Broker error code returned (e.g. NOT_ENOUGH_REPLICAS, OUT_OF_ORDER_SEQUENCE_NUMBER)
Missing or dropped records (sum of high watermarks != acked records)
Connection reset, broken pipe, or unhandled socket timeout
Client panic, SIGSEGV, unhandled exception, or unexpected termination
Progress strings without verified end-to-end completion
Latency sample count below declared sample floor
